 Series Notes
 Phoenix swept Sacramento 4-0 last season, winning two at home and two on the road
 The Suns have won five of their six most recent meetings against the Kings
 Key Connections
 Kings center Mason Plumlee played the 2024-25 season in Phoenix, appearing 74 times (21 starts) and averaging 4.5 points and 6.1 rebounds
 Suns AC Jesse Mermuys held the same position with the Kings from 2019-21 under Luke Walton
 Kings AC Leandro Barbosa played nine season with the Suns from 2003-10, 2013-14 and 2016-17, averaging 11.7 points, 2.4 assists and 2.2 rebounds in 553 games (109 starts) ... Barbosa ranks 9th in franchise history in games played (553) and 4th in three-point field goals (751)

 #3 – Dillon Brooks LAST GAME : Played 22 minutes and recorded 2 rebounds
 Recorded 20 points in the first half vs. Denver on Oct. 30, his ninth career first half with 20+ points
 Named Western Conference Player of the Week (Jan. 26 to Feb.1), his first career NBA honor, averaging 28.8 points, 4.5 rebounds and 2.8 assists
 #22 – Miles Bridges LAST GAME : Totaled 14 points, 3 rebounds and 3 assists
 Totaled 135 points, 65 rebounds and 29 assists in his first eight games with Phoenix, the fifth Suns player to do so through their first eight games with the franchise

 #1 1– Oso Ighodaro LAST GAME : Ended with 4 points, 2 rebounds and 3 assists
 Played in all 82 games with Phoenix in 2025-26, the first Suns player to do so since 2021-22

 #4 – Jalen Green LAST GAME : Posted 9 points and 2 steals

 #15 – Devin Booker LAST GAME : Put up 17 points, 7 assists and 4 rebounds
 Turned 30 years old on Oct. 30, exiting his 20's with the 11th most points in NBA history by any player before their 30th birthday

 Notes
 The Suns ended their seven-game homestand with a 131-123 loss against the Lakers on Nov. 15. Phoenix went 4-3 during the stretch and the contest was the first leg of its third back-to-back of the season.
 COLLIN GILLESPIE put up a team and season-high 26 points (8-of-14 FG, 5-of-10 3FG), 4 assists and 4 rebounds. His 26 points were his third-most in a game in his NBA career. Gillespie doubled his points total in the fourth quarter after entering the frame with 13 points. His 13 points in the final frame were the most by a Suns player in the fourth quarter this season. Gillespie knocked down five triples for the 13th time of his career and first time this season. It marked the most points by a Suns reserve since Grayson Allen’s 28-point performance on Feb. 26 against the Lakers last season.
 LUKE KENNARD ended with 18 points (7-of-14 FG), his most in a Suns uniform, to go along with 6 rebounds and 4 assists. He now has six games with 3+ threes this season, all coming off the bench. Kennard ranks tied for second amongst all reserves in the category this season. His six rebounds were a new season high.
 JORDAN GOODWIN recorded 14 points, 7 rebounds, 6 assists, a steal and a block. He is the first Suns reserve since Rodney Rogers in 2000-01 to post those numbers in a contest.
 Playing just eight minutes, KOA PEAT tallied 10 points (5-of-7 FG) and 2 rebounds. His 10 points are a new career high. Peat posted six consecutive points for the Suns to help bring Phoenix back into the contest in the fourth quarter. He is the first Suns rookie to score 10 points in under 10 minutes since Tyler Ennis in 2014-15.
 Team Leaders by Points Per Game
 24.8 pts Devin Booker 15 | G 14.6 pts Miles Bridges 22 | F 13.8 pts Dillon Brooks 3 | GF See more stats Last Game Recap
 PHOENIX - The Suns (5-7) ended their seven-game homestand with a 131-123 loss to the Lakers on Nov. 15. Luka Dončić tallied 20 points in the first quarter for Los Angeles, who got out to a quick 23-5 advantage. Phoenix ended the frame down by nine points as Devin Booker tallied another 10-point first quarter this season. A closer second quarter ensued, ending with the Lakers up by 10 points at the break. Los Angeles posted a dominant third quarter out of halftime, dropping 40 points off the back of 23 combined points from Dončić and Quentin Grimes. The Lakers built their lead to 31 points before the Suns went on a strong run powered by their bench. Phoenix cut into Los Angeles' advantage, trailing by just six points with under five minutes left in the game. Collin Gillespie topped all scorers with 13 points in the final period. Gillespie, who ended with a season-high 26 points and five three-pointers, was joined by rookie Koa Peat as the two Suns in double figures in the fourth quarter. The Suns won the fourth quarter 43-27, forced six turnovers and tallied 15 points off those turnovers.
